objectives: Build fluency through repeated controlled reading.
concepts: A word family shares a common rime.
Onset-rime awareness supports efficient word recognition.
Controlled text limits patterns to taught correspondences.
Fluency requires accuracy, smoothness, and meaning.

definitions.definition: A group of words sharing a common rime pattern.
The vowel and sounds that follow the onset in a syllable.
Text designed to use taught decoding patterns and vocabulary.

commonMistakes: Guessing a family word from context.

conceptual: Compare shared rimes and identify outliers.
application: Read controlled sentences and answer literal questions.
higherOrderThinking: Explain how repeated rime patterns support fluent decoding.
mixedReview: Mix /g/ word-family recognition with controlled reading.

quickRevision: notice rime → decode → read sentence → reread
formulaOrFactBank: Word-family fluency grows when the shared rime becomes automatic while the onset is decoded accurately.
mistakeBasedRevision: Return to the onset and rime when a family word is misread.
weakTopicRevision: Practise the specific word family that remains slow or inaccurate.

outcomes: Learner improves fluency through rereading without losing meaning.

questions.question: Which word belongs to the -ag family?
Which word belongs to the -ig family?
Which word belongs to the -ug family?
Read: “Gus has a bug.” What does Gus have?
Read: “Gag has a bag.” Which word names the object?
Read: “A big bug is on a rug.” What is big?
A learner reads every -ag word accurately but struggles with -ig words. What should be practised?
Which word does not belong with bag, gag, and tag?
Why does reading a word family help fluency?
options: It lets the learner notice a repeated rime pattern quickly.
It removes the need to decode.
It teaches every word by picture.

questions.question: Which strategy supports accurate controlled reading?
options: Blend unfamiliar words and reread the sentence smoothly.

questions.question: After reading “Gus has a big bug,” which rereading goal is best?
options: Read accurately, smoothly, and with meaning.
Read as fast as possible with errors.
